body:
PATCH /settings actually has PUT semantics: accounts.update_settings() writes
BOTH columns on every call, so a request carrying only default_currency resets
a custom initials override to NULL (reproduced: set initials "CZ", PATCH
currency-only → initials silently back to the derived default), and a request
carrying only initials 422s on the missing currency.

Both clients currently work around it by always resending both fields (web
SettingsPage, Android SettingsViewModel — each carries a "must resend" comment,
which is the tell that the server semantics are wrong). The workaround has a
real hole on Android: the initials preload is best-effort (offline start →
initials stays ""), and a later currency save then resends "" and wipes the
user's override.

Fix server-side: treat an absent key as "leave unchanged" (validate only the
keys present; distinguish absent from explicit null for initials, where null =
clear override). Also validate the initials type (a non-string currently hits
len() → 500). Then drop the client workarounds (or leave them — they become
harmless).

Files: server/src/shoppinglist_server/accounts.py,
server/src/shoppinglist_server/routes/account.py, server/tests/test_account.py;
optional cleanup: web/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx,
android .../ui/settings/SettingsViewModel.kt.
title: Server: PATCH /settings behaves as PUT — currency-only PATCH wipes the initials override
